title: Panama Papers — who structures the network

reports.title: How to read this dashboard
reports.query:
Degree is counted live in this database. An intermediary's degree is the number of entities it points to with INTERMEDIARY_OF. An officer's degree is the number of OFFICER_OF links. An entity's degree adds its officers, its intermediaries, and its registered addresses. Degree centrality divides that number by n − 1 = 468,622.

The tallest officer bar is THE BEARER (degree 70,850), then EL PORTADOR (9,325). Those are bearer-share placeholders, not named people. The largest named officer is MOSSFON SUBSCRIBERS LTD. at 3,958.

PageRank and betweenness are on the next pages. Those scores come from the NetworkX notebook, stored as :CentralityScore. Graph Data Science is installed on this server; the course report still uses the notebook.

reports.title: Entities
reports.query: MATCH (n:Entity) RETURN count(n) AS value

reports.title: Officers
reports.query: MATCH (n:Officer) RETURN count(n) AS value

reports.title: Intermediaries
reports.query: MATCH (n:Intermediary) RETURN count(n) AS value

reports.title: Addresses
reports.query: MATCH (n:Address) RETURN count(n) AS value

reports.title: Highest-degree intermediaries
reports.query:
MATCH (i:Intermediary)-[:INTERMEDIARY_OF]->(e:Entity)
WITH i.name AS name, count(e) AS degree
ORDER BY degree DESC
LIMIT 12
RETURN CASE WHEN size(name) > 42 THEN substring(name, 0, 41) + '…' ELSE name END AS name, degree

reports.title: Highest-degree officers
reports.query:
MATCH (o:Officer)-[:OFFICER_OF]->(e:Entity)
WITH o.name AS name, count(e) AS degree
ORDER BY degree DESC
LIMIT 12
RETURN CASE WHEN size(name) > 42 THEN substring(name, 0, 41) + '…' ELSE name END AS name, degree

reports.title: Highest-degree entities
reports.query:
MATCH (e:Entity)
WITH e,
  COUNT { (e)<-[:OFFICER_OF]-() } +
  COUNT { (e)<-[:INTERMEDIARY_OF]-() } +
  COUNT { (e)-[:REGISTERED_ADDRESS]->(:Address) } AS degree
ORDER BY degree DESC
LIMIT 15
RETURN e.name AS name, e.jurisdiction AS jurisdiction, degree,
       toFloat(degree) / 468622 AS degree_centrality

reports.title: Entities by jurisdiction
reports.query:
MATCH (e:Entity)
WITH e.jurisdiction AS jurisdiction, count(*) AS entities
ORDER BY entities DESC
LIMIT 10
RETURN jurisdiction, entities

reports.title: Share of entities and share of links, by jurisdiction
reports.query:
MATCH (e:Entity)
WITH e, COUNT { (e)<-[:OFFICER_OF]-() } + COUNT { (e)<-[:INTERMEDIARY_OF]-() } + COUNT { (e)-[:REGISTERED_ADDRESS]->(:Address) } AS degree
WITH e.jurisdiction AS jurisdiction, count(*) AS entities, sum(degree) AS degree_sum
WITH sum(entities) AS n, sum(degree_sum) AS d, collect({jurisdiction: jurisdiction, entities: entities, degree_sum: degree_sum}) AS rows
UNWIND rows AS row
RETURN row.jurisdiction AS jurisdiction,
       row.entities AS entities,
       toFloat(row.entities) / n AS share_of_entities,
       toFloat(row.degree_sum) / d AS share_of_links
ORDER BY entities DESC
LIMIT 12

reports.title: Where these scores come from
reports.query: PageRank, damping 0.85, calculated in NetworkX on the undirected bipartite graph and on the largest component of the capped entity projection. A score of about 0.000002 is an average node on the bipartite graph. The bars are the raw PageRank of the top intermediaries. The projection drops connectors above the cap, so the giant intermediaries are not nodes there.

reports.title: Intermediaries by PageRank
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'pagerank', kind:'intermediary'})
RETURN CASE WHEN size(n.name) > 42 THEN substring(n.name, 0, 41) + '…' ELSE n.name END AS name, n.score AS pagerank
ORDER BY n.rank

reports.title: Officers by PageRank
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'pagerank', kind:'officer'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS countries, n.score AS pagerank
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Entities by PageRank, bipartite graph
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'pagerank', kind:'entity'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS jurisdiction, n.score AS pagerank
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Entities by PageRank, projection component
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'projection', measure:'pagerank', kind:'entity'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS jurisdiction, n.score AS pagerank
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Sampling
reports.query: Exact betweenness would start a shortest-path search from every node. On the bipartite giant component that is about 311,000 starts, which does not finish in NetworkX. These scores use 50 random sources on that component and 200 sources on the projection component, seed 0, distances in hops. Read the top of each list. A small gap between two mid-ranked names is not a reliable difference.

reports.title: Intermediaries by betweenness
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'betweenness', kind:'intermediary'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS countries, n.score AS betweenness
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Officers by betweenness
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'betweenness', kind:'officer'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS countries, n.score AS betweenness
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Entities by betweenness, projection component
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'projection', measure:'betweenness', kind:'entity'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS jurisdiction, n.score AS betweenness
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Orion House and 40 of its entities
reports.query:
MATCH (i:Intermediary)-[r:INTERMEDIARY_OF]->(e:Entity)
WHERE i.name STARTS WITH 'ORION HOUSE SERVICES'
WITH i, r, e
LIMIT 40
RETURN i, r, e

reports.title: Jurisdictions of Orion House clients
reports.query:
MATCH (i:Intermediary)-[:INTERMEDIARY_OF]->(e:Entity)
WHERE i.name STARTS WITH 'ORION HOUSE SERVICES'
RETURN e.jurisdiction AS jurisdiction, count(*) AS entities
ORDER BY entities DESC
LIMIT 8

reports.title: Where the firm sits, and where the company is registered
reports.query: Each bar is a route from the intermediary's country to the jurisdiction of the company it set up. Hong Kong firms incorporate 27,131 British Virgin Islands companies, the largest route. Switzerland is next, into the British Virgin Islands (16,855) and Panama (10,497). The agent and the shell are usually in different countries.

reports.title: Largest routes, firm country to company jurisdiction
reports.query:
MATCH (i:Intermediary)-[:INTERMEDIARY_OF]->(e:Entity)
WHERE i.countries IS NOT NULL AND e.jurisdiction IS NOT NULL
WITH split(i.countries, ';')[0] AS firm_country, e.jurisdiction AS company_jurisdiction, count(*) AS entities
ORDER BY entities DESC
LIMIT 12
RETURN firm_country + ' → ' + company_jurisdiction AS name, entities AS value

reports.title: The same routes as a table
reports.query:
MATCH (i:Intermediary)-[:INTERMEDIARY_OF]->(e:Entity)
WHERE i.countries IS NOT NULL AND e.jurisdiction IS NOT NULL
WITH split(i.countries, ';')[0] AS firm_country, e.jurisdiction AS company_jurisdiction, count(*) AS entities
ORDER BY entities DESC
LIMIT 12
RETURN firm_country, company_jurisdiction, entities

reports.title: Names that stand in for an owner
reports.query: THE BEARER is a bearer share, not a person: whoever holds the paper owns the company. Officers with that name are attached to 70,850 companies. EL PORTADOR is the same device in Spanish, on 9,325 companies. MOSSFON SUBSCRIBERS LTD. in Samoa is the largest named nominee, on 3,958 companies. The graph shows 40 of that nominee's companies.

reports.title: How many companies hide behind each name
reports.query:
MATCH (o:Officer)-[:OFFICER_OF]->(e:Entity)
WHERE o.name IN ['THE BEARER', 'EL PORTADOR', 'MOSSFON SUBSCRIBERS LTD.']
RETURN o.name AS name, count(e) AS value
ORDER BY value DESC

reports.title: 40 companies of Mossfon Subscribers Ltd.
reports.query:
MATCH (o:Officer {name:'MOSSFON SUBSCRIBERS LTD.', countries:'Samoa'})-[r:OFFICER_OF]->(e:Entity)
WITH o, r, e
LIMIT 40
RETURN o, r, e

reports.title: One building, several spellings
reports.query: Akara Building, 24 De Castro Street, Wickhams Cay, Road Town, Tortola is a Mossack Fonseca shelf address. It is stored as four different strings and those four nodes alone are the registered address of about 3,170 officers and companies. A shared address is a mail drop, not evidence that the holders work in the same room. The graph shows 40 of the holders of the most common spelling.

reports.title: Addresses used by the most holders
reports.query:
MATCH (n)-[:REGISTERED_ADDRESS]->(a:Address)
WITH a, count(n) AS holders
ORDER BY holders DESC
LIMIT 12
RETURN CASE WHEN size(a.name) > 42 THEN substring(a.name, 0, 41) + '…' ELSE a.name END AS name, holders AS value

reports.title: 40 holders of Akara Building
reports.query:
MATCH (a:Address) WHERE a.name STARTS WITH 'AKARA BLDG.; 24 DE CASTRO STREET'
MATCH (n)-[r:REGISTERED_ADDRESS]->(a)
WITH a, r, n
LIMIT 40
RETURN a, r, n

reports.title: Who sits on the paths between companies
reports.query: Betweenness estimates how often a firm lies on a shortest path between other nodes. It was sampled in the notebook, 50 sources on the giant component. Mossack Fonseca Singapore is first (0.150) and the UK office is second (0.135). Orion House has the largest client book but ranks third (0.098). Singapore and the UK connect groups of companies that otherwise do not meet. The graph shows 40 companies of the Singapore office.

reports.title: Intermediaries by betweenness
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'bipartite', measure:'betweenness', kind:'intermediary'})
RETURN CASE WHEN size(n.name) > 42 THEN substring(n.name, 0, 41) + '…' ELSE n.name END AS name, n.score AS value
ORDER BY n.rank

reports.title: 40 companies of Mossack Fonseca Singapore
reports.query:
MATCH (i:Intermediary) WHERE i.name STARTS WITH 'MOSSACK FONSECA & CO. (SINGAPORE)'
MATCH (i)-[r:INTERMEDIARY_OF]->(e:Entity)
WITH i, r, e
LIMIT 40
RETURN i, r, e

reports.title: Companies tied by a smaller shared officer
reports.query: The entity projection links two companies when they share an officer, an intermediary, or an address, and it ignores a connector above the cap. Giant firms such as Orion House therefore disappear, and PageRank promotes a different set of companies. Four of the top five are a Bahamas block: Follet Corporation, Iceland Management, Alpine Investments, and Lovena Investments. The graph draws Follet Corporation and the Bahamas companies that share one of its officers.

reports.title: Entities by PageRank on the projection
reports.query:
MATCH (n:CentralityScore {graph:'projection', measure:'pagerank', kind:'entity'})
RETURN n.rank AS rank, n.name AS name, n.extra AS jurisdiction, n.score AS pagerank
ORDER BY rank

reports.title: Follet Corporation and its Bahamas neighbors
reports.query:
MATCH (e:Entity {name:'FOLLET CORPORATION'})<-[r1:OFFICER_OF]-(o:Officer)-[r2:OFFICER_OF]->(other:Entity)
WHERE other.jurisdiction = 'Bahamas' AND other <> e
RETURN e, r1, o, r2, other
